newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Train services halted to Kindu over Zaire war.
newsitem.headline: Train services halted to Kindu over Zaire war.

text.p: Zaire's Cizarail train company has suspended all traffic to the eastern town of Kindu and evacuated staff and equipment in case of rebel attack, a senior Cizarail director said on Wednesday.
Kindu, a key transport hub on the Zaire River and a declared target of rebel leader Laurent Kabila, is the northernmost working station on a rail line to South Africa.
Cizarail sources said the town was deserted on Tuesday after residents fled fearing a rebel attack.
The Cizarail director said there had been no radio contact with the town since Tuesday, after materials and some personnel were evacuated.
"Since all the other services had evacuated we too followed. It is a preventive measure to protect our materials," he said.

Cizarail is owned partly by Belgian and South African interests and partly by the Zairean state. It is a vital route for mining exports and for food and other imports to the vast south eastern region.
Zaire's defence ministry said on Wednesday it had beaten back a rebel advance on the town, killing hundreds of rebels in an ambush 35 km (22 miles) further east.
There was no independent confirmation and independent sources spoke of Zairean soldiers looting in some parts of town.
